sourcing.title: Trusted Sourcing
sourcing.text: We work directly with trusted suppliers in Japan, French Polynesia, and Australia — including renowned names like Mikimoto and Paspaley. Every pearl is hand-selected for its luster, surface quality, and shape. Our gold and silver hardware is sourced from Japan, where strict regulations on gold content ensure every component is genuinely solid — never hollow, never cut with base metals.

gold.title: 18K Solid Gold
gold.text: More than 70% of our pieces are set in solid 18K gold — the ideal balance of purity, durability, and warmth. Precision-crafted in Japan, where stricter gold regulations guarantee every setting is solid all the way through. It will not tarnish or cause skin reactions with regular wear.

silver.title: 14K Gold & Japanese Silver
silver.text: For a more accessible price point, select pieces are crafted in solid 14K gold or Japanese silver finished with gold plating. Our silver is worked using a Japanese technique that makes it noticeably more resistant to tarnish than standard silver, so it stays bright with everyday wear.

pearls.title: Pearl Types
pearls.akoya: Akoya pearls from Mie Prefecture, Japan — prized for their mirror-like luster and perfect round shape.
pearls.tahitian: Tahitian black pearls from French Polynesia — naturally dark, ranging from charcoal to deep green.
pearls.southsea: South Sea pearls from Australia — the largest and rarest, with a satiny, luminous glow.

care.title: Pearl Care
care.intro: Pearls are organic gems and deserve gentle care. Follow these guidelines to keep yours beautiful for generations.
tips: Put pearls on last — after perfume, hairspray, and makeup.
Wipe with a soft, damp cloth after wearing.
Store flat in a soft pouch or lined box, away from other jewelry.
Avoid ultrasonic cleaners, steam, and harsh chemicals.
Re-string knotted pearl necklaces every few years with regular wear.

q2.question: What materials do you use?
answer: We use 18K gold as our standard setting material — high quality, hypoallergenic, durable, and it holds its value.
Current pieces include necklaces, earrings, ear clips, bracelets, and rings. Over 50% of our findings are Japanese-made for quality and longevity.
For diamond-set pieces, you can choose between cubic zirconia, lab-grown diamonds, or natural diamonds. Pricing varies accordingly.

q3.question: What pearl types do you carry, and what's the difference between saltwater and freshwater?
answer: Saltwater pearls have brighter luster and more stable structure — ideal for pieces you'll wear for years. Freshwater pearls are more affordable but differ in luster and durability.
We primarily carry high-quality saltwater pearls sourced directly from Japan:

items: Akoya (Japan)
South Sea (Australia)
Tahitian Black (French Polynesia)

answer: A good pearl isn't just for one season — it stays beautiful for years, even decades.
Freshwater pearls have their charm, but if you're looking for something that truly stands the test of time, we'll honestly recommend saltwater.
